Model type: Proposed supervised three-layer feed-forward ANN; one binary output node; training/testing deferred
Inputs: 20 proposed inputs listed in Section 5; measured and calculated surface/downhole variables
Outputs: Failure-directed operating condition versus suitable operation
Reported performance: Not reported. No dataset size, holdout results, confusion matrix or validated warning time.
Advantages: Combines heterogeneous component limits and operating patterns.
Limitations: Conceptual study; incomplete feature equations; several threshold/unit/comparator errors; model-specific inputs and extensive downhole/design data required.
Data feasibility: Avalon alone: not established. Combined Avalon, test and surface-pressure data: insufficient without equipment ratings, fluid properties and valid downhole/calculated features. Surface-only version would be a new model.
Prediction target: Potential adverse operating conditions; neither remaining life nor failure date demonstrated.
Lead time qualification: Not reported.
Signals: Twenty proposed inputs plus component limits.
Source thresholds: Source thresholds appear in Section 6 and must retain ambiguity flags.
Implementation proposal: Start with reviewed rated-limit checks; quarantine contradictory thresholds; collect adjudicated failures before training the ANN.
Recommended future model: Future failure-risk classifier with component metadata and labeled run histories; reduced-sensor retraining needed.

Model type: Hybrid pump physics plus pooled random forest and per-well linear regression; weighted prediction of increments; constrained grid search
Inputs: Current state, lagged/smoothed state, historical changes, proposed frequency change, static/pump data and economic data
Outputs: Post-change critical parameters, production response and recommended frequency/duty
Reported performance: One-sided intake-pressure prediction error ≤2.4×10^4 kg/m² for 99% of source cases; no full-model accuracy statistic. Production uplift 1.5% is not accuracy.
Advantages: Increment prediction reduces slowly varying reservoir measurement bias; pooled model supports sparse individual histories; uncertainty included.
Limitations: Stable wells only; blending confidence algorithm undisclosed; network interference and equivalent injection unresolved; geologist approves settings; sample-count/pressure-unit discrepancies.
Data feasibility: Avalon alone: no. Combined three user sources: partial; need static equipment/fluid metadata, valid downhole CIPs, insulation, energy/prices and reservoir context. Injection response not solved.
Prediction target: Response to control changes and constraint crossing; not validated remaining life.
Lead time qualification: Motor response 2–3 hours and intake response 5–10 days; no failure horizon.
Signals: State, history, CIPs, production, pump model and metadata.
Source thresholds: Field-specific values and unit discrepancy in Section 6.
Implementation proposal: First implement data-quality and stability gates, then shadow-test recommendations with uncertainty and human approval; use tests to verify incremental oil.
Recommended future model: Hybrid response-to-frequency model; duty-cycle optimizer; later network and producer–injector optimization.

Model type: Spreadsheet fuzzy inference; triangular memberships; product AND, OR and Most-of coupling; rank DOF directly without separate defuzzification
Inputs: Eight daily-median trend variables; slopes normalized with arctangent
Outputs: Scores for nine failure-mode hypotheses and possible generic risk indication
Reported performance: No validated accuracy. System did not identify actual root causes in five failures. Many zero premises defeated product AND; Most-of remained low. Table 2 includes example scores, not probabilities.
Advantages: Transparent and spreadsheet-compatible; offshore dataset and explicit rule matrix.
Limitations: Nine selected wells; actual causes not established; scale/unit-sensitive arctangent; common memberships; trip contamination; three identical rule vectors; 30/60-day gaps.
Data feasibility: Avalon+production+surface-pressure data could support full rules only where all eight inputs exist. Lost PIP/PDP/temperature makes published rules incomplete; do not replace missing conditions by true.
Prediction target: Possible developing distress/risk, not specific failure or RUL.
Lead time qualification: 7/30/60 days are analysis windows, not proven warning lead times.
Signals: Eight signals plus event masks and confirmed outcomes.
Source thresholds: Figure 3 prints D=(-100,-0.6,-0.2), C=(-0.5, 0, 0.5), I=(0.2, 0.6,100). Curve shoulders and text's triangle notation need careful implementation; no validated alert DOF threshold.
Implementation proposal: Implement as explainable hypothesis scores, with unit-consistent slopes, event segmentation and missing-signal coverage; validate specificity before operational use.
Recommended future model: Unit-aware fuzzy risk triage; learned membership functions; comparison with supervised failure labels.

Model type: Generic multilayer neural networks, Python/TensorFlow; one model per ESP variant; cloud anomaly monitoring
Inputs: Annulus and production pressure, current, speed, intake pressure, intake temperature, motor temperature
Outputs: Anomaly indication described probabilistically; human selects mitigation
Reported performance: No accuracy, recall, precision or false-alarm rate reported. One 12-day retrospective warning; qualitative pilot success.
Advantages: Learns normal relationships and can flag unfamiliar patterns; independent SCADA validation.
Limitations: Architecture/training details undisclosed; causality unclear; manual baseline cleansing; unknown anomalies hard to interpret; repeated historical tuning risks optimism.
Data feasibility: Avalon plus surface pressures can supply some inputs if tags exist; published model still needs three downhole channels. Production tests alone are insufficient. Reduced-sensor model requires separate training/validation.
Prediction target: Abnormal operation potentially preceding failure; not a verified failure mode or exact date.
Lead time qualification: 12 days in one historical case; hours-to-days threshold tradeoff.
Signals: Seven synchronized inputs, variant and historical events.
Source thresholds: Source examples >80% and <40%; not proven probabilities or field alarm settings.
Implementation proposal: Train on adjudicated healthy regimes, hold out complete wells/runs, score in shadow mode, calibrate false alerts and provide evidence to engineers.
Recommended future model: Normal-behavior anomaly detector with separate sensor-available and surface-only versions.

Model type: Robust PCA (configured for 25% outliers), T² surveillance, contribution diagnostics, quadratic conditional operating bands
Inputs: 22 measured/derived variables; one-minute historian plus event records
Outputs: Health trajectory, scalar anomaly score, ranked contributions and suggested stable bands
Reported performance: >96% explained variance is not detection accuracy. All studied events reportedly detected hours early; event denominator/false-positive rate and independent prospective test not supplied.
Advantages: Interpretable visual trajectory and contributors; relatively modest mathematical complexity.
Limitations: Linear normal model; correlated data; anonymized inputs; fixed-other-variable bands are not causal control policy; no held-out performance counts.
Data feasibility: Full replication requires downhole/thermal/vibration/leakage data and unnamed tags. A reduced Avalon+surface-pressure model is feasible as a new validated model; sparse production tests add context, not minute-scale signals.
Prediction target: Developing multivariate instability preceding some trips.
Lead time qualification: Hours; one illustrated ~30-hour interval.
Signals: Historian variables, event log and clean healthy baseline.
Source thresholds: 95% F-distribution boundary; figure example T² boundary near 10, not transferable.
Implementation proposal: Build regime-specific robust PCA with run-state masks, contributor display, persistence and false-alert evaluation; keep recommendation assessment outside raw contribution ranking.
Recommended future model: Robust PCA baseline for sensor-rich wells, separate surface-only baseline, later fault classifier.

Model type: Neural-network normal-behavior/anomaly model; architecture not disclosed
Inputs: Historical and real-time ESP KPIs, unnamed
Outputs: Anomaly/failure likelihood described conceptually
Reported performance: One 12-day retrospective example; no sensitivity, specificity, calibration or false-alert figures.
Advantages: Fleet triage and unfamiliar-pattern detection.
Limitations: Two-page guest editorial; no reproducible model specification or independent results; probable same Siemens case as P04/P36.
Data feasibility: Cannot determine from unnamed inputs. Do not assume lost-sensor compatibility.
Prediction target: Possible failure-associated anomalies.
Lead time qualification: 12 days in one example, not guaranteed.
Signals: Undisclosed process KPIs.
Source thresholds: None reported.
Implementation proposal: Use as a concept entry and trace implementation evidence to technical papers, without treating it as an independent validation.
Recommended future model: Normal-behavior model concept only; use stronger papers for design.

Model type: Ada BNet (Ada Boost+Bayesian networks) and Ada DT (Ada Boost+decision trees)
Inputs: 14+ daily rod-pump attributes with expert preprocessing and normalization
Outputs: Normal, tubing failure, rod failure and pre-signal classes
Reported performance: Narrative reports Ada BNet normal 97.7%, failure 91.9%; Table 3 has transposed/inconsistent labels/count orientation. Ada DT ~95% best at 80–180 iterations. Training-table 'percent' entries are actually fractional-looking errors; do not reproduce as <0.12% without correction.
Advantages: Single field model rather than one per well; well-level evaluation.
Limitations: Rod systems; recorded-date bias; missing-data fill; table inconsistencies; claimed proof of no overfitting contradicted by reported overfit above 180 iterations; record-level CV may leak within wells.
Data feasibility: No direct ESP implementation with Avalon/tests/pressures: rod card/load inputs missing. General workflow transferable.
Prediction target: Rod-system failure states and pre-signals, not validated ESP failures.
Lead time qualification: 2/8-month examples reference recorded dates, not verified physical onset.
Signals: Rod load/card/production/runtime and adjudicated event labels.
Source thresholds: Learned model votes; no transferable engineering limits.
Implementation proposal: Transfer evaluation/label discipline only; establish ESP-specific features, whole-run temporal holdout and alert-event matching.
Recommended future model: Boosted classifier benchmark after complete ESP retraining.

Model type: Neural-network anomaly analytics on centralized Io T cloud with multiuser HMI
Inputs: ESP historical/real-time process data; not enumerated
Outputs: Anomaly severity, notifications and fleet priority list
Reported performance: No numerical model performance or warning time; continuation of earlier Siemens work.
Advantages: Shared evidence, scalable triage and explicit advisory/control separation.
Limitations: Architecture-level treatment; root causes and model mechanics undisclosed; availability of unknown downhole inputs not resolved.
Data feasibility: User sources can support an analogous architecture, but cannot establish exact model replication or sensor-loss performance.
Prediction target: Abnormal behavior requiring review.
Lead time qualification: Not quantified here.
Signals: Quality synchronized process history; full list not disclosed.
Source thresholds: Not reported.
Implementation proposal: Build read-only evidence-backed fleet triage in Copilot, keep existing control/protection workflow and measure alert usefulness.
Recommended future model: Fleet anomaly ranking service feeding Copilot; specific model requires other evidence.

Model type: Deterministic feature extraction and pattern matching: normalized mean, variance, thresholds, frequency features and waveform correlation
Inputs: Six surface signal groups with dynamic per-well reference patterns
Outputs: Nine operating conditions including normal
Reported performance: Qualitative laboratory/field suitability claim; no confusion matrix, sample count or numerical accuracy.
Advantages: Explicitly designed without downhole measurements; interpretable combined signatures.
Limitations: Several table/text contradictions; diagrams schematic; current waveform sampling requirement unspecified; live gas/liquid meter unlike intermittent tests; pressure formulas dimensionally ambiguous.
Data feasibility: Combined Avalon+tests+surface pressure supports a reduced screening version if time aligned; exact method requires real-time gas/liquid sensing and waveform fidelity. Avalon alone insufficient for differential diagnosis.
Prediction target: Current operating-condition diagnosis; no demonstrated failure-date or RUL prediction.
Lead time qualification: Not reported.
Signals: Current, voltage, real-time gas/liquid rates, GLR, surface pressure.
Source thresholds: Normal current ±5%; illustrative normalized 0.8/1.2; site calibration required; correlation threshold undisclosed.
Implementation proposal: Implement as ranked hypotheses with test age/coverage visible; collect event-rate electrical data and confirm with fresh tests before causal advice.
Recommended future model: Surface-only interpretable classifier; current waveform matching plus production context.

Model type: Linear-kernel SVM with domain-engineered daily features and sliding-window ratios; hyperparameters cross-validated
Inputs: Current, voltage, frequency, runtime and quality/event labels
Outputs: Normal versus anomaly/inefficiency
Reported performance: Overall precision 61.8%, recall 61.5%; FMT1 62.5%/70%; FMT2 50%/33.3%. Separate years used for train/test; hundreds of wells. TP-I event recall and TP-II alert precision use ±90-day matching and differ in counting.
Advantages: No downhole sensor needed; fleet normalization and practical electrical features.
Limitations: Labels subjective; inefficiency versus failure confused; 90-day window can inflate usefulness; no fixed RUL; copying prior data can manufacture patterns.
Data feasibility: Avalon alone conditionally sufficient for scoring if four raw tags and history exist; event/maintenance labels still needed for training. Tests/surface pressures useful for diagnosis, not original inputs.
Prediction target: Anomalous/inefficient state associated with future reported events.
Lead time qualification: 90 days is evaluation tolerance, not demonstrated per-event warning time.
Signals: Electrical, runtime, quality and confirmed events.
Source thresholds: Site maximum current for cleaning; no universal failure thresholds; SVM boundary learned.
Implementation proposal: Strong surface-only baseline candidate; retain missingness, mask planned cycling, evaluate chronological run-held-out event precision/recall and false alerts per well-month.
Recommended future model: Surface-only linear SVM or tree benchmark using electrical/runtime features.

Model type: Attribute forward selection; linear/polynomial regression and neural-network life regression
Inputs: Primarily static equipment/geometry/production, sand proxy and operating-cycle duration
Outputs: Pump service life/MTBF-type estimate
Reported performance: ESP R²: linear 0.71, neural network 0.81; beam 0.10/0.12/0.29. R² is not classification accuracy. Authors do not recommend general deployment due to limited data.
Advantages: Integrates heterogeneous records; interpretable factor priorities.
Limitations: Post-pull HUD risks target leakage; censoring treatment and held-out validation unclear; correlated feature weights are not causes; only failure cases may bias life model.
Data feasibility: Three sources alone insufficient: need installations/pulls/failure labels, completion geometry, equipment and contemporaneous solids data. Downhole sensors not essential to original static model.
Prediction target: Service-life estimate conditional on recorded attributes.
Lead time qualification: No early-warning horizon; post-pull predictor compromises prospective use.
Signals: Static metadata, operation cycles, production and valid pre-event solids metric.
Source thresholds: No ESP alarm thresholds. Beam geometry recommendations must remain separate.
Implementation proposal: Assemble run-level dataset including censored survivors; replace HUD leakage; validate survival/life models on later installations.
Recommended future model: Survival model and run-life regression with contemporaneous inputs; failure-report extraction.

Model type: RUL: linear/ridge/lasso/DT/RF/GB/XGBoost/KNN/LSTM/ANN; horizon classification LR/DT/GB/XGB/RF/KNN/ANN/PCA+RF; failure type DT/GB/XGB/RF/KNN/CNN/ANN/SVM, one-vs-all and resampling variants
Inputs: Electrical, hydraulic, fluid/test, static configuration and history features; target labels must be excluded from inputs
Outputs: Days-to-next-failure, 30/14/7/1-day flags and ten classes: F-cable SC, high water cut, human error, motor SC, penetrator SC, pump shaft broken, pump stuck, R-cable SC, tubing leak, WO
Reported performance: Table 49 RF R²=.9897, MAE 12.02 d; KNN .9727/19.03 d; ANN .9752. Table 52 30 d RF precision .81/recall .96/F1 .88; KNN .88/.91/.90; ANN .12/.87/.21. Table 53 RF baseline 99.84% accuracy versus SMOTE+Tomek 82%. These are different experiments, not a single validated deployment score. Chronological ANN reported R² .94/.95 with RMSE 227.8 d; source acknowledges collapse of many random-split models.
Advantages: Large feature/taxonomy inventory, comparative models, explicit discussion of leakage and rare-class metrics.
Limitations: Conflicting cohort/metric tables, ambiguous split nomenclature, backward filling and full-well imputation risk lookahead, supervised failure clustering may require unavailable future mode, censoring handling unclear, post-event labels mixed with causal categories and WO. Claimed R² '4.0' is invalid as a conventional positive upper-bound score and likely missing a sign; retain as source error.
Data feasibility: Avalon+tests+surface pressures insufficient alone: installation/failure/DIFA/configuration/chemistry needed. Models include downhole channels; missing-sensor imputation is not independently validated as a virtual sensor.
Prediction target: Candidate RUL, horizon risk and failure class; cause attribution framework separate from prediction.
Lead time qualification: 30-day risk labels preferred in source; 1/7-day precision weak. Case 12-day and 30–90-day claims are not robust prospective guarantees.
Signals: Full as-of feature set, run boundaries, event labels, censoring and sensor-coverage flags.
Source thresholds: 30/14/7/1-day label horizons; z/IQR data screens; hours-online ≤24 and study choke cap 128/64 inch are data checks, not universal operating alarms.
Implementation proposal: Rebuild raw-to-feature pipeline with no backward future fill, per-run temporal holdouts/purge, censored survivors and external field tests; compare 30-day RF against simple electrical baseline before RUL.
Recommended future model: 30-day calibrated RF benchmark, survival/RUL model with censoring, hierarchical cause-assistance model only after label audit.

Model type: Random forests for failure events; CNN dynacard descriptors; shallow trees/RF for suboptimal states; generalized supervised workflow
Inputs: Rod controller, pressure, load, fillage, dynacard and event labels
Outputs: Fault/suboptimal-event classes and scores
Reported performance: Tubing test accuracy .995, precision .546, hourly recall .421; event detection 80/133=60.2%, 66 false interventions. Pump CV precision .714, accuracy .875, recall .996; event detection 113/172=65.7%, 45 false interventions. CNN descriptor precision/recall vary .596–.955/.651–.983. These are rod results; abstract >99% does not describe all models.
Advantages: Whole-well CV, event aggregation, explicit false interventions and quality gates.
Limitations: Rod-specific features; imbalance (~1% failure time) inflates accuracy; retrospective labels use later evidence; cannot use those future observations live; small suboptimal-event cohorts.
Data feasibility: No direct ESP reproduction from Avalon/test/pressure sources; methodology transfers after new ESP features/labels. Gas-lift extension is not water-injection evidence.
Prediction target: Rod failure/suboptimal states; ESP extension proposed.
Lead time qualification: 31-day life-estimation error in abstract is not warning time; no validated ESP lead.
Signals: Rod-specific six core signals and event labels.
Source thresholds: Model scores .5/.75; eligibility 4 h/50 d, not ESP alarm limits.
Implementation proposal: Transfer data eligibility, whole-well/time holdouts and event-level alert accounting to an ESP pilot.
Recommended future model: ESP event detector using own electrical/production features and whole-event scoring.

Model type: Descriptive failure statistics, chi-square association and Cramér’s V; no trained predictive AI in this article
Inputs: Failure/DIFA records and contextual operational data
Outputs: Two-level taxonomy, frequency rankings, associations and API-code crosswalk proposed by authors
Reported performance: No ML accuracy. Reported chi-square 342, df 324, p=0.2356; grouped Cramér’s V=0.16. This supports weak association, not causal certainty.
Advantages: Useful structured labels and distinction between failures and operational removals.
Limitations: Incomplete RCA, selection/subjective reporting, weak association, counts and category counts not perfectly consistent; counterfactual economics and unsupported discussion percentages.
Data feasibility: Avalon/tests/pressures support evidence but not confirmed root causes; DIFA, workover and installation records essential. Sensor loss does not prevent taxonomy use.
Prediction target: No validated forecast; improved labels enable future models.
Lead time qualification: Not reported.
Signals: Failure and DIFA evidence plus matched operating history.
Source thresholds: No validated sensor alarm thresholds; generic thermal-aging statements are not ESP-specific trip settings.
Implementation proposal: Adopt separate symptom/mode/component/cause/evidence-status fields; retain unknowns and non-failure pulls; later train only on adjudicated histories.
Recommended future model: NLP-assisted failure-report labeling; hierarchical mode classifier followed by evidence-based cause ranking; no causal certainty from SHAP/frequencies.

Model type: Simulink multiphysics twin; synthetic data generator; future hybrid AI module
Inputs: Detailed asset/fluid/reservoir/completion metadata and live telemetry
Outputs: Full signal simulation, latent residuals, training signatures; diagnosis/RUL are intended AI capabilities
Reported performance: No field predictive accuracy, residual threshold or RUL error. AI module and field prototype/trials are future work.
Advantages: Couples thermal/electrical/hydraulic behavior; represents transients; synthetic fault coverage.
Limitations: Calibration/identifiability, uncertain physics, sim-to-real gap; stochastic life assignment is not observed RUL; no deployed validation.
Data feasibility: Three user data sources alone insufficient without equipment, completion, fluid and reservoir model. Virtual sensing for missing downhole channels is an opportunity, not demonstrated accuracy here.
Prediction target: Simulated response and synthetic fault signatures; future RUL/diagnostic capability.
Lead time qualification: Not reported.
Signals: System metadata, telemetry and calibration references.
Source thresholds: No operational alarm limits; two-minute simulation target is computational cadence.
Implementation proposal: Begin with calibrated hydraulic/electrical residuals and independent tests; add thermal model and missing-sensor estimates with uncertainty before full twin.
Recommended future model: Virtual sensor with uncertainty; hybrid residual classifier; synthetic-data augmentation tested on real withheld runs.

Model type: Two random forests with engineered physics/statistical features
Inputs: 35 raw channels reduced to 18; static completion/install/failure records; means, differences, SD and calibrated virtual rates/efficiencies. Three years used because physics-derived history limited.
Outputs: Binary well failure next 30 days; pump failure next 45 days.
Reported performance: Initial well test: TP55, FN42, TN96, FP1; precision 98.2%, recall 56.7%, accuracy 77.8%. Pump test: TP6, FN4, TN21, FP1; precision 85.7%, recall 60%, accuracy 84.4%. Blind 35-well review: well TP17, FN12, TN27, FP2 => precision 89.47%, recall 58.62%, accuracy 75.86%. Pump TP12, FN6, TN28, FP1 => precision 92.31%, recall 66.67%, calculated accuracy 85.11%; paper prints 88.11% and 39 correct although matrix has 40 correct (p.20).
Advantages: Physics features and separate component target; blind wells; high positive predictive value in study.
Limitations: Small component sample, SME-corrected event dates, balanced initial test prevalence and retrospective review. Roughly 40% well failures missed. Complete 18-feature names not disclosed.
Data feasibility: Not directly from three stated sources alone: requires completion/equipment/failure records and validated physical models; missing downhole sensors remove important inputs. Reduced-signal model requires separate training.
Prediction target: Aggregate failure risk and pump-component risk.
Lead time qualification: Nominal 30/45 day labels; historical blind averages about 60 days are a different measurement, with broad ranges including 0 days for well failures.
Signals: Measured telemetry, physical model outputs, maintenance/install outcomes.
Source thresholds: No operational risk cutoff disclosed. >75% data quality over 120 days is a training gate.
Implementation proposal: Reconstruct independent ESP-run timelines, causal features and physical models; prospective shadow alerts; measure event precision/recall, false alarms per well-month and lead distributions.
Recommended future model: Hybrid physics plus tree model, separately validated for full-sensor and surface-only cohorts.

Model type: Gradient-boosted tree ensembles using XGBoost, CatBoost and Light GBM tool families; source reports horizon models rather than a fully reproducible winner configuration.
Inputs: 1153 wells, 2070 failures 2014–2020; daily measurements; 30 variables consolidated 9; derived UNIFLOC hydraulic/power features, 85% separation assumption; time statistics and cumulative work.
Outputs: Failure probability at 1, 2, 3, 7, 14 days.
Advantages: Large fleet, held-out 20% wells(397 test failures), physical preprocessing improves results.
Limitations: Balanced 50/50 class evaluation; interpolated/imputed values are not recovered measurements. Akima≤5 day gaps and long-gap moving-average/linear fills may use future data unless made causal. Component/manufacturer/stage metadata unavailable.
Data feasibility: Needs equipment, trajectory, PVT, failure records and physical model beyond three sources. Surface-only version is a new experiment, not established by results.
Prediction target: Aggregate failure risk, strongest near-term horizon.
Lead time qualification: 1–3 days supported more strongly than 7–14 days. This is forecast-label horizon, not demonstrated maintenance lead for every event.
Signals: Daily telemetry, production context, resistance, physics and exposure features.
Source thresholds: Probability .5 in balanced classification; not a fleet-calibrated operating alarm.85% separation is a modeling assumption.
Implementation proposal: Use strictly past-only filling; show missingness; split by run/well/time; recalibrate for rare actual failures and compare measured-only versus inferred-feature models.
Recommended future model: Short-horizon boosting with measured-only and physics-assisted ablations.

Model type: Robust PCA and Hotelling T-squared statistical monitoring
Inputs: Two years of minute data, 22 variables; robust treatment of roughly 25% outliers.
Outputs: Health KPI and abnormal operating-state alerts.
Reported performance: Six PCs explain>96% variance; two explain about two-thirds. These are variance-retention figures, not detection accuracy. No sensitivity/specificity/event denominator.
Advantages: Can learn normal behavior without labeled failures; compact dashboard.
Limitations: Limited illustrated cases; no validated causal diagnosis; 95% pointwise bound does not equal 5% fleet event false-alarm rate; operating regime shifts matter.
Data feasibility: Potential with mapped Avalon channels; full reproduction requires 22 inputs, whose complete names are not disclosed. Missing-sensor cohort must use its own baseline. Excel tests are context, not minute inputs.
Prediction target: Departure from normal multivariate operation.
Lead time qualification: Case-specific hours; no population warning distribution or RUL.
Signals: Consistent synchronized multichannel telemetry.
Source thresholds: 95% confidence bound on T-squared; model-specific, not physical trip.
Implementation proposal: Fit healthy regime-specific baselines; exclude startup/shutdown transients as appropriate; require persistence and contribution review; evaluate false alerts and event detection.
Recommended future model: Robust PCA baseline as interpretable comparator to more complex models.

Model type: Streaming change/anomaly detection; PCA; linear regression/least median squares; trapezoidal/Gaussian fuzzy trend inference; influence-diagram decision ranking.
Inputs: Core 8 channels and operating/economic context.
Outputs: Detected event, candidate cause and ranked prescriptive message.
Reported performance: Five illustrative cases: plugged pump, fluid change, gas lock, tubing leak, no alert. No confusion matrix, statistical accuracy or validated lead distribution.
Advantages: Explicit interpretable patterns and practical action alternatives; field bacterial blockage and gas-control examples.
Limitations: Membership thresholds not fully reproducible; overlapping pump patterns; experimental percentages not universal limits; no sensitivity/specificity.
Data feasibility: Full matrix cannot run on sensor-lost wells. With Avalon electrical channels and sparse Excel only, retain partial-evidence hypotheses and request missing checks; no fabricated PIP/PDP or live rate.
Prediction target: Abnormal operating conditions; paper demonstrates detection/prescriptive support, not calibrated RUL.
Lead time qualification: Not established.15/30 min and 24/48 h thresholds are observation windows.
Signals: Core 8 channels plus optional vibration/discharge temperature/rating/curves.
Source thresholds: PIP change: absolute daily-average PIP change >=5% in 24 h; Rapid motor temperature rise: motor temperature increases >=10% over 30 min; Wellhead pressure change: absolute daily-average WHP change >5% in 24 h; Unstable intake/current: PIP standard deviation changes >20% over 24 h; Rapid discharge change: absolute PDP change >=20% over 15 min; Discharge thermal rise: absolute daily-average discharge temperature change >=7% over 48 h; Vibration increase: vibration >20% above installation baseline; High motor loading: motor amps >=90% nameplate at 60 Hz; Loading change: motor loading changes >25% over time; Specific-energy deterioration: source specific-energy/lift metric differs >15% from as-installed; Worn versus plugged head curve: head curve lower over operating range
Implementation proposal: Implement source-qualified candidate rules with data/frequency gates; retain multiple causes; score evidence completeness; display approved checks and verified operational limits.
Recommended future model: Fuzzy diagnostic ranking; trend/change-point detector; outcome-based ranking of engineer-approved interventions.

Model type: ADTree, SVM, naive Bayes; Grubbs outlier test, LOWESS, robust polynomial trends; random-peek semi-supervision.
Inputs: Daily LOWIS measurements; 42 training wells(19 failure), 32 reported test wells(6 failure); intermittent tests carried forward.
Outputs: Normal versus pre-failure.
Reported performance: Held-out SVM TP5, FN1, FP10, TN17 => precision 33.3%, recall 83.3%; ADTree TP1, FN5, FP5, TN22 =>precision 16.7%, recall 16.7%. Both matrices total 33 although text says 32. Table 2 SVM failure error.017, normal.002, overall.026 cannot all be consistent weighted error.
Advantages: Robust trends; distinguishes failure and normal error; adaptation to test-well distribution.
Limitations: Very small event count; random-peek uses unlabeled test distribution (transductive evaluation); high false alarms; inconsistent counts/metrics; smoothing may erase real events.
Data feasibility: No direct ESP reproduction from Avalon/Excel; card/load/rod variables absent. Can reuse causal feature engineering and event-based evaluation design.
Prediction target: Rod pump/tubing failure patterns.
Lead time qualification: One-month examples; evaluation counts alarms within 60 days.14 day/7 day windows are features, not lead.
Signals: Dynamometer/load/runtime and outcome records.
Source thresholds: ADTree negative score; no transferable physical cutoff.
Implementation proposal: For ESP build fresh features; avoid interpreting random-peek test adaptation as untouched prospective validation.
Recommended future model: Robust trend classifier benchmark after ESP-specific redesign.

Model type: EM Gaussian-mixture labeling plus physical-rule filtering; multiclass RBF SVM.
Inputs: 1947 rod pumps, five fields; train 2010, validate 2011; four primary trends plus card unchanged days/runtime ratio.
Outputs: Normal, pre-failure and failure classes for tubing/pump.
Reported performance: TP278, FP145, FN141, TN1383 =>precision 65.7%, recall 66.4%. Field precision 50.0–80.2%, recall 47.1–88.5%. Historical evaluation; deployment future work.
Advantages: Cross-field training and chronological holdout; documents sudden failures cannot be anticipated from absent trends.
Limitations: 100 day matching tolerance; alerts within 15 days of downtime filtered; different fields vary markedly; prose incorrectly labels false positive as false negative; normal-cluster cutoff 70% prose versus 50% algorithm.
Data feasibility: Rod-card variables absent in ESP sources; methodology transferable only after new ESP training/labels.
Prediction target: Trend-bearing rod pump/tubing failures; abrupt rod/joint events not reliably forecast.
Lead time qualification: 100 day evaluation tolerance is not proven 100 day advance warning; actual failure may precede recorded discovery.
Signals: Load-card/runtime series and independent event dates.
Source thresholds: 100 nonmissing signatures; normal cluster>50% algorithm versus 70% prose; tubing-card shrinkage lambda unspecified.
Implementation proposal: Use source methodology to design cross-well ESP study; audit true onset vs discovery date and report abrupt-event detection separately.
Recommended future model: Global ESP classifier with well/time holdout and cohort-specific performance.

Model type: Deterministic engineering algorithms and virtual performance indicators; not trained ML.
Inputs: Pump curves, density, PI, electrical/downhole/surface variables.
Outputs: Envelope, motor load, rate estimates and prioritized relax/restrict/rerating candidates.
Reported performance: No prediction accuracy or false-alarm statistics.4.6 year run life is operational reported outcome, not controlled effect.
Advantages: Transparent and practical; basic/medium/high instrumentation tiers.
Limitations: Rate/head inference requires density and calibration; claimed benefits lack control cohort.
Data feasibility: Basic electrical surveillance feasible if tags mapped. Full hydraulic envelope needs valid downhole pressures or independently validated estimates plus curves/PVT/completion data outside three sources.
Prediction target: Off-envelope operation and impending trip risk; no RUL prediction.
Lead time qualification: Not quantified.
Signals: Telemetry plus curves/nameplates/fluid data.
Source thresholds: Local curve limits and nameplates; 60→80% loading is an example, not alarm threshold.
Implementation proposal: Start with electrical/rating dashboard, add pressure-based duty for instrumented wells, display uncertainty for sensor-lost wells.
Recommended future model: Physics-based virtual rate/efficiency; constrained optimization as later stage.

Model type: DNN(36 time/frequency features)+two CNN branches(STFT, CWT128×128 RGB) fused to 5 class softmax.
Inputs: Manufacturer laboratory water tests; 36 accelerometers over 6 components; 4096 Hz.9690 stated samples.
Outputs: Normal, unbalance, misalignment, rubbing, sensor fault.
Reported performance: Reported mean accuracy~99.98%; Table 6 recall 100% exceptmisalignment 99.93%; AUC100% reported. Class counts 3774+2703+1938+969+255=9639, not 9690; split 7752/1938 matches 9690. Repetition count 10 versus 25 intext.
Advantages: Combines complementary waveform representations and explicitly distinguishesensor fault.
Limitations: Labwater data; random record split may share machine/test run signatures; no held-out field run validation or predictive lead; high training cost.
Data feasibility: No, unless Avalon contains raw 4096 Hz waveforms with correct positions. HF operating telemetry is not automatically vibration waveform data. Excel sources cannot substitute.
Prediction target: Present mechanical/sensor fault class; future failure not validated.
Lead time qualification: Not reported.
Signals: Raw accelerometers and speed.
Source thresholds: No physical alarm cutoffs; spectral roll off.85 is feature definition.
Implementation proposal: Confirm waveform availability; first run simple spectral/baseline classifiers; split by physical unit/test run before investing in deep fusion.
Recommended future model: Laboratory/bench QA classifier or field waveform classifier after data acquisition.

Model type: PCA+XGBoost; hourly median, 1.5 IQR filter, standardization, moving differences.
Inputs: 339089 normal, 1728 preworkover, 288 workover hourly points; 8 physical signals+differences.
Outputs: Normal versus≤7 day pre-event; discussion uses normal/preworkover/workover classes.
Reported performance: 10 fold mean ROC-AUC.95; test pre-event precision.80, recall.60, F1.71, support 604; normal 101726. Abstract says>0.71, table.71.
Advantages: Clear physical polymer mechanism and explicit imbalanced-class metrics.
Limitations: 70/30 versus 70/15/15 split descriptions; random folds not well/run chronological validation; full-data PCA/scaling language risks leakage; tables contain impossible descriptive ordering(mean/std versus max); standardization text says variance rather than SD.
Data feasibility: Full model needs downhole sensors and workover labels. Three sources alone insufficient unless labels/equipment context supplied. Sensorless variant untested.
Prediction target: Electrical preworkover state.
Lead time qualification: ≤7 day label; point recall 60% does not equal 60% event recall or guaranteed 7 day warning.
Signals: Eight synchronized signals, causal moving differences, independent failure/workover records.
Source thresholds: 1.5 IQR is cleaning threshold, not fault limit; no physical operating cutoff.
Implementation proposal: Preserve genuine extremes; fit transforms on training only; chronological ESP-run holdout; report event recall, alarm duration, lead and false alerts.
Recommended future model: PCA+boosting benchmark alongside raw-feature boosting, full sensor and surface-only cohorts.

Model type: Gaussian-kernel SVR with genetic-algorithm tuning of C, epsilon, kernel width; ten input combinations.
Inputs: J200 N test circuit, 1800/3000 rpm, inlet 100/200 bar, gas 0–3 kg/h; 80/20 train/test.
Outputs: Gas mass flow estimate.
Reported performance: Best total-flow+head model MSE .0027 (~.003), reported correlation .997. Vibration-only MSE .022, correlation .983; flow-only .930/.597. Units/scaling of MSE need source-data verification.
Advantages: Demonstrates value of combining hydraulic signals; vibration not required for best laboratory model.
Limitations: Narrow test domain; no offshore validation, failure outcomes or RUL; head/elevation is not simply well depth. Some estimates negative at zero gas.
Data feasibility: Not directly: continuous total flow and developed head at matched conditions required. Sparse surface tests and no downhole sensors do not reproduce these inputs; requires PVT/calibrated hydraulic model and gas-reference labels.
Prediction target: Gas mass flow soft sensor, not future failure.
Lead time qualification: None established.
Signals: Total flow and developed head preferred; optional raw vibration/torque.
Source thresholds: Source introduction says gas-oil ratio should not exceed 10%; definition/dimensions ambiguous and pump-specific—do not use as universal gas fraction trip.
Implementation proposal: Calibrate against multiphase measurements and physical head calculation across local speed/fluid domain; reject extrapolation and negative unphysical outputs.
Recommended future model: Physics-assisted gas-flow/void-fraction estimator after obtaining suitable reference data.

Model type: Proposed LSTM/ANN with min-max scaling and 70/30 split.
Inputs: Field surveillance and X/Yvibration; sample table 52 Hz; record counts, architecture and event labels insufficiently specified.
Outputs: Pump discharge pressure prediction interpreted as failure warning.
Reported performance: No numeric RMSE, classification precision/recall, confusion matrix or lead-time validation. Qualitative plotted fit/correlation claim only.
Advantages: Sequence modeling concept and multichannel data assembly.
Limitations: Assumes build-up failure mechanism; instantaneous failures acknowledged; no non-Newtonian rheology validation or quantified predictive evidence; table lacks units.
Data feasibility: No reproduction without downhole pressure/temperature/vibration and fuller model specification. Surface-only performance not demonstrated.
Prediction target: Pressure trajectory hypothesis, not established failure/RUL.
Lead time qualification: Not reported.
Signals: Pressure, current, speed, temperature, vibration histories.
Source thresholds: 30–70 Hz stated as typical range, 52 Hz case; neither is universal operating limit. No validated alarm threshold.
Implementation proposal: Use only as low-priority concept; define physical target and causal validation before LSTM development.
Recommended future model: Pressure residual forecasting only after simpler physics/tree benchmarks.

Model type: PCA to 3 dimensions plus least-squares enclosing sphere.
Inputs: 13 variables, 20 min samples, 174538 stable records from 47 wells; 40 normal comparison wells use daily report data.
Outputs: Stable versus anomalous/failure trajectory.
Reported performance: TP20, FN27, TN40, FP0; event recall 42.55%, calculated overall accuracy 68.97%, observed precision 100% in this small selected sample. Paper calls 42.5%'accuracy' but it is failure recall.3 PCs retain~70% variance.
Advantages: Simple interpretable healthy-boundary monitor; explicitly reports missed failures.
Limitations: Normal/failure sampling resolution differs; only 70% variance retained; 20 min samples miss fast dynamics; same wells contribute healthy/failure periods; small selected normal set.
Data feasibility: Needs 13 inputs including downhole signals and choke. Sensor-lost model requires new baseline and separate validation; daily Excel context does not recreate 20 min telemetry.
Prediction target: Some developing faults; abrupt failures may only be detected.
Lead time qualification: Unquantified; 20 events before recorded failure.
Signals: 13 synchronized channels with mode/quality metadata.
Source thresholds: Maximum training distance, not physical safety limit.
Implementation proposal: Use high-frequency Avalon data and regime-specific baselines; compare PCA residual/SPE and T² with sphere; test independent runs and record false alerts per operating hour.
Recommended future model: PCA baseline with both retained-space and residual-space monitoring.

Model type: Standardized PCA2 D plus Azure two-class boosted decision tree screenshot.
Inputs: 8 variables abstract versus 10 Dmethod; 3 failed+1 operating case; tree 70/30 split.
Outputs: Normal/failed status and PCA drift.
Reported performance: PCA PC1=78.47%, PC2=9.94%, total 88.41% variance, not accuracy. Screenshot positive class NORMAL: TP441, FN0, FP14, TN56; accuracy.973, precision.969, recall 1, F1.984, AUC.927. Recast failure-positive: TP56, FN14, FP0, TN441 =>failure recall 80%, precision 100% in reported sample.
Advantages: Direct sensor-loss/ground-fault examples and frequency-conditioning lesson.
Limitations: Small cases; automatic real-time deployment future work; tree labels/sample independence unspecified; months-long retrospective drift can reflect onset/discovery ambiguity.
Data feasibility: Full PCA unavailable after downhole loss; build separate surface baseline. Electrical integrity/DIFA/metadata are additional required records.
Prediction target: Deteriorating multivariate behavior, especially electrical cases; no validated RUL.
Lead time qualification: Well A drift April 2018, failure June 2018(~2 months), source says 3 months; Well B failure-region May 2016 precedes March 2017 sensor issue 10 months and August 2017 terminal failure; not transferable forecast horizon.
Signals: Frequency-specific telemetry and quality/electrical integrity records.
Source thresholds: Tree.5; source typical undervoltage 20% off nameplate requires actual OEM/site settings. No universal PCA radius.
Implementation proposal: Keep sensor loss separate from physical fault; retain mode-specific baseline; independently test surface-only model and alert-to-confirmed-fault timing.
Recommended future model: Sensor-availability-aware anomaly models and electrical degradation risk.

Model type: RCFA and descriptive reliability trending; no ML.
Inputs: Operating/design/material/DIFA/history records.
Outputs: Evidence-supported root cause and preventive action.
Reported performance: No diagnostic accuracy. MTBF chart 196,190,168,292,254,628 days for 1995–2000; active runs require censoring in formal reliability analysis.
Advantages: Directly actionable evidence and prevention workflow.
Limitations: Small field, concurrent interventions, ambiguous improvement percentages/economic units.
Data feasibility: Avalon+Excel support surveillance but not full RCFA; needs DIFA, materials, chemistry, settings, installation records.
Complexity: Low for workflow; Medium for integrated reliability analysis
Prediction target: Recurring risk/exposure and duty mismatch, not individual failure time.
Lead time qualification: Not quantified.
Signals: Telemetry plus design and forensic records.
Source thresholds: No universal numerical warning. Biweekly data review and quarterly optimization are source practices.
Implementation proposal: Create ESP-run/DIFA taxonomy linking initiating cause, mechanism, failed part and corrective action; verify effectiveness on subsequent runs.
Recommended future model: Repeat-failure risk and censored survival analysis once DIFA/run history cleaned.

Model type: Bayesian/HMM-like piecewise signal segmentation (top 200 paths), trend/noise/correlation probabilities, expert Bayesian network with manually/equation-set CPTs.
Inputs: Minute telemetry and physical/reference knowledge.
Outputs: Probabilities of stress patterns and failures.
Reported performance: 57 field/offline events: 37 low flow, 12 deadhead, 6 gas, 2 mechanical; 14 missed by engineer, 10≥1 h earlier, 1 wrong diagnosis later addressed, 32 same-time. Additional 22 proof-of-concept=>79 total; no independent healthy-time denominator or fleet false alarm rate.
Advantages: Interpretable uncertainty and explicitly limited missing-input handling.
Limitations: Reference tuning after frequency change;~5% unusual wells require tuning; incomplete sensors+unusual conditions degrade accuracy; 57 event selection does not prove universal 100% recall.
Data feasibility: Some partial-sensor cases supported, 17/79 events with≥1 missing parameter. Loss ofboth PIP/PDP violates source crucial-input gate; surface-only cannot claim this method's diagnostic performance.
Prediction target: Stress-pattern detection before possible damage; existing fault diagnosis.
Lead time qualification: 10/57 events≥1 h before engineer report; stress-to-failure time not calibrated.
Signals: Eight core inputs with quality/reference context.
Source thresholds: ~75% event probability; trend threshold examples~40% strong change,~5% wear; sensor-resolution-specific noise limits.
Implementation proposal: Implement explainable candidate logic first; calibrate priors locally, abstain on missing critical evidence; measure alarm workload and confirmed outcomes.
Recommended future model: Bayesian diagnostic ranking and causal change-point feature extractor.

Model type: BP neural network 45 inputs–15 hidden–10 outputs plus analytical pressure-buildup model.
Inputs: Field and synthetic current cards; abstract training across>900 wells; at least 50 simulated examples per class; 45 features from 24 h cards; hydraulic model needs fluid/completion/pump curve.
Outputs: Ten current-card classes plus hydraulic diagnosis.
Reported performance: No held-out aggregate accuracy. Case output 57% normal, 12.3% sand failed to identify leak; pressure method led to confirmed tubing leak.
Advantages: Directly addresses absence of downhole sensors using additional surface test evidence.
Limitations: Synthetic training and validation not fully characterized; current classes overlap; Figure 5 rendering partly corrupted; empirical 0.78/1.5/1 cutoffs not universal.
Data feasibility: Current features possible from Avalon; full pressure method needs dedicated time-resolved test and extra completion/PVT/curve data. Routine Excel pressures/tests alone insufficient.
Prediction target: Present operational class and integrity/performance fault; no validated RUL.
Lead time qualification: No quantified advance warning; 24 h card is lookback.
Signals: Current plus engineered WHP response and physical model.
Source thresholds: Pressure ratio 0.78/1.5, current ratio 1; learning rate.4 is model setting, not field alarm.
Implementation proposal: Use production-current mismatch as screening; retain multiple causes; implement pressure interpretation only for approved acquired tests with uncertainty.
Recommended future model: Current-pattern classifier with verified field labels; hybrid hydraulic integrity classifier.

Model type: Per-ESP PCA T² versus XGBoost motor-vibration regression residual with SPC aggregation.
Inputs: Six failed ESPs>1 year history; initial windows grown 20,000 min to 210,000 min; preferred 180,000 min~125 days; sequential 80/20 within-window validation for regression.
Outputs: Abnormal minute/day and persistent failure advisory.
Reported performance: Table 1 PCA false alarms 1, 4, 0, 3, 5; leads 14, 7, 1, 1, 3 days (first 5). Nonlinear false alarms 1, 11, 12, 10, 6; leads 14, 41, 10,120, 13. Sixth poor-quality well: PCA19 false/2 days, nonlinear 2 false/327 days, excluded from averages. No classification accuracy or independent nonfailure cohort.
Advantages: Chronological per-well construction and explicit alarm persistence tradeoff.
Limitations: Six failed wells only; parameter selection retrospective; no fleet rate denominator; two-day persistence delays fast faults; real-power proxy I×V omits three-phase power factor/efficiency.
Data feasibility: PCA needs pressure/rate/temperature; residual method requires measured vibration at scoring, not just surface predictors. Cannot calculate residual after losing vibration sensor.
Prediction target: Persistent abnormal operation or earlier recognition of existing failure.
Lead time qualification: Abstract~2 weeks; detailed means 5/40 days. Source explicitly says one event already catastrophic for 14 days before confirmation—do not label all lead as prevention time.
Signals: Synchronized minute telemetry, actual vibration for residual method, independent onset/confirmation dates.
Source thresholds: PCA nominal tail.0027; residual.01;>12/>195 minutes daily and 2 days persistence. These statistical assumptions are not valid fleet guarantees under autocorrelation.
Implementation proposal: Tune causal alarm persistence by fault urgency; preserve fast protective systems; count missing minutes separately; validate on healthy and failed runs.
Recommended future model: Vibration residual benchmark only on wells retaining reliable vibration.

Model type: Meta-learning convolutional shrinkage symptom model; semantic/fault trees; Jaccard entity linking; graph subgraph ranking; BiLSTM-CRF and expert inference, choosing higher-confidence result.
Inputs: 1373 offshore fault records over 10 years; 7398 sentences from 62 papers+10 annual reports; 14 series; 27 symptoms; 50 claimed fault classes; 70/15/15 record split 961/206/206; separate 80/20 meta-stage description.
Outputs: Ranked fault candidates and confidence.
Reported performance: Recall@3=93.35%, reported macro F1=89.93%, time 35.5 (unit not explicit in table). LSTM73.26/83.26/33.2; KG-BDA88.10/87.74/37.9. Not 93.35% top-one accuracy. Warning/alarm table 38.3/32.6 versus 42.9/32.8 without sufficiently clear timing definition.
Advantages: Surface-based inputs; explicit symptoms, candidates and explanation; knowledge helps sparse classes.
Limitations: Restricted private data/graph; hard exclusions physically overbroad; random event split not external-field validation; equation 8 accuracy omits TN and F1 derivation inconsistent; confidence scores from two models may be incomparable; exact 50-label taxonomy not cleanly enumerated.
Data feasibility: Potentially close to project, but requires continuous surface channels, plant rate-estimation method, verified fault labels and graph. Sparse Excel tests cannot substitute for minute production estimates. No downhole sensors required by core input set.
Prediction target: Current fault diagnosis/ranking; early recognition of some progressing conditions.
Lead time qualification: Not established as a transferable forecast horizon.30–60 min general assertion is not evidence for all ESP failure modes.
Signals: Surface electrical/pressure/temperature plus reliable rate estimates and metadata.
Source thresholds: Normalized>1 termed overload, cap 1.5; normal-reference exceedance is not equipment-rated overload. Partial associations/exclusions retained for audit, not approved rules.
Implementation proposal: Start with curated symptoms and soft candidate ranking, not full architecture; keep alternatives, unknown state and evidence provenance; validate independent wells and calibrated confidence.
Recommended future model: Knowledge-assisted surface classifier after reliable rate/label integration.

Model type: Linear regression, decision tree and logistic regression at multiple time scales.
Inputs: Geology/trajectory plus whole-run or current-period summaries; 42 paired failure/non failure periods; all-period set 29 fail/891 nonfail.
Outputs: Total life, active hours-to-failure and period failure probability.
Reported performance: Geology+geometry R².41(adj.38); hours-on regression R².75(adj.73), tree.82. Paired classifier TP30, FN12, FP18, TN24=>recall 71.43%, precision 62.5%. All-period fitted TP25, FN4, FP1, TN890=>recall 86.21%, precision 96.15%, but evaluated on fitting data; authors acknowledge optimism and unsuccessful small-data validation.
Advantages: Distinguishes calendar time, active exposure and failure versus other stops.
Limitations: Completed-run summaries leak future information if used as prospective predictors; only 29/42 failure cases; correlated features; no reliable external validation or forecast lead.
Data feasibility: Surface concepts transferable, but SAGD steam/injector/geological inputs absent from stated sources. Ordinary water injection cannot substitute for SAGD steam variables.
Prediction target: Exploratory lifetime association and final-period failure classification.
Lead time qualification: Not quantified; source explicitly describes some predictions as failure happening.
Signals: Current-defined periods, independent event labels and operating context.
Source thresholds: Tree cutoffs are fitted retrospective partitions, not control settings.
Implementation proposal: Use past-only rolling exposure; retain censored runs and competing shutdown reasons; assess survival models with independent future runs.
Recommended future model: Censored survival/competing-risk model with past-only operating exposure.

Model type: Isolation Forest→PCA5 PCs→CatBoost/ExtraTrees with temporal features; SVM/MLP comparators; SMOTE/class weights reported.
Inputs: One selected well of 7,105 day window, 87390 raw records; 83020 final prose versus 82350 table; 30 s claimed sampling.
Outputs: Rule-derived three-state class.
Reported performance: Abstract accuracy 94.2%, failure recall 96.5%; Table 9 CatBoost 99.85% accuracy/F1~99.83%; Table 10/11 CV97.2% accuracy, F1~97.2%; ExtraTrees 96.8% test/93.8% CV. These are distinct conflicting reports, not one validated score.
Advantages: Useful past-window trend features and comparison of practical tabular models.
Limitations: One well, selected anomalous window; labels depend on same signals as features; no independent event-level prospective validation; chronological versus stratified K-fold descriptions conflict; preprocessing/SMOTE placement unclear; outlier removal may discard true faults; claimed 5 PC variance 90/95/97% inconsistent.
Data feasibility: Requires working downhole pressure/temperature/vibration; surface voltage/current prior to transformer must not be treated as motor-terminal values. Missing-sensor version untested.
Prediction target: Operational state according to retrospective rules; superiority in future failure prediction not established.
Lead time qualification: No validated forecast horizon; 2–4 h/1 h conditions and 4 h plots are not demonstrated advance warning.
Signals: Eight physical variables plus causal engineered trends and independent outcomes.
Source thresholds: 90°C,.02 g delta,−100 psi/min are study-specific and internally inconsistent with distribution; not approved ESP limits.
Implementation proposal: Benchmark direct rules against trees using independent DIFA/trip labels; fit preprocessing within training folds; grouped chronological holdout and event-level alarms; preserve genuine anomalies.
Recommended future model: CatBoost/ExtraTrees benchmark with independently labeled future events, including raw-feature ablation.

Model type: Generic multilayer neural-network anomaly detector; architecture/loss not disclosed.
Inputs: 30 onshore ESPs, 200–500 k W; equipment variants grouped; one-year normal training baseline; surface/downhole telemetry.
Outputs: Anomaly level and prioritized advisory.
Reported performance: 12 day retrospective example; no precision, recall, confusion matrix, false alerts per well-month or independent event denominator.
Advantages: Learns complex normal relationships; can highlight previously unrecognized anomalies.
Limitations: Manual training-data curation; repeated tuning on same history; missing cause specificity; limited reproducibility; related publications reuse pilot evidence.
Data feasibility: Potential Avalon-fed monitoring, but full published model uses downhole inputs. A sensor-lost cohort requires new baseline and validation; Excel tests supply contextual evidence rather than fast stream.
Prediction target: Abnormal behavior preceding some interruptions; not RUL or unique cause.
Lead time qualification: One 12 day case; no guaranteed horizon.
Signals: Seven process variables plus quality/event records.
Source thresholds: ~80% versus<40% anomaly-score examples; final operating cutoff undisclosed.
Implementation proposal: Pilot in advisory mode with cohort-specific baseline and prospective event/alert audit; compare simple PCA/tree baselines before deep model.
Recommended future model: Normal-behavior multivariate anomaly model per sensor/equipment cohort.
